title: 第二章　布尔什维克对日记的看法

children: 苏维埃自我改造的革命工程具有“苏维埃宗教改革”的特征。
的确，布尔什维克对在全境传播意识和将这种意识作为个人经验的双重强调，让人联想起宗教改革时期的教会创造个体化信仰的努力。16世纪的宗教改革和苏维埃革命都具有主体化倾向——它们都呼吁创造自立的主体：就宗教改革而言，这些主体要监督自己的灵性健康；就苏维埃而言，他们则要把自己理解为负有历史使命的政治主体。
The Soviet revolutionary project of self-change had features of a “Soviet Reformation.”

Indeed, the Bolsheviks’ double emphasis on spreading consciousness throughout the realm and on making this consciousness a matter of individual experience recalls the efforts of the Reformation church to create an individualized faith. Both the sixteenth-century Reformation and the Soviet revolution had a subjectivizing thrust—they called for the creation of self-reliant subjects, who in the case of the Reformation were to monitor their spiritual health, and who in the Soviet case were to comprehend themselves as political subjects with a historical mission.

宗教改革使日记作为改革后基督徒灵魂的账簿而传播开来。作为一种个人和社会实践，日记在清教徒新英格兰炽热的宗教氛围中获得了特别显著的地位。清教徒牧师把记日记当作一种为救赎而自我修行的方式，也当作传播信仰的手段。他们的自传文学既是个人的，也是规范性的。它是个人的，因为朝圣与冲突、磨难与恩典的主题，是日记作者经验的反映和自我意识的产物。但它也是规范性的，因为这种文体被接受为一种模范框架，在此框架内“虔诚生活的基本模式”被铭刻和成形，“[个人的]经验在此框架内被理解。”

清教徒日记主要不是被看作仅供作者本人审视的私密记录。日记发挥了作者自身救赎工具的作用，并在此程度上支持了个人独特性的观念，但清教徒圣徒在写下自己的忏悔时，始终设想着公众读者。对于清教徒来说，个人与民族的重生发生在迈向救赎的共同朝圣中。这种在追求救赎的过程中使主观的个体自我与集体相一致的做法，强烈地让人联想起苏维埃通过加入革命将个人的主观意识提升到客观真理水平的观念。苏维埃共产党人是否同样利用日记作为其意识形态总体化与个体化的手段？

The Reformation led to a dissemination of the diary as an account book of the reformed Christian’s soul. As an individual and social practice, the diary gained particular prominence in the fervent religious climate of Puritan New England. Puritan ministers adopted the technique of diary-keeping as a way to work on the self in the service of salvation and as a means of disseminating their faith. Their autobiographical literature was personal and prescriptive at the same time. It was personal, in that the themes of pilgrimage and conflict, of trouble and grace, were reflections of the diarist’s experience and products of his self-consciousness. But it was also prescriptive, in that the genre was accepted as a model frame within which the “basic patterns of the godly life” were to be inscribed and take shape, and “within which [an individual’s] experience was to be understood.”

The Puritan diary was not conceived of primarily as an intimate record to be scrutinized by the author alone. The diary functioned as an instrument of its author’s own salvation and to this extent supported notions of personal individuality, but Puritan saints always kept a public audience in mind while producing their confessions. For the Puritans, personal and national regeneration took place in a shared pilgrimage toward salvation. This alignment of the subjective, individual self with the collective in the pursuit of salvation is strongly reminiscent of the Soviet conception of the raising of individuals’ subjective consciousness to the level of objective truth through their joining of the revolution. Did Soviet Communists likewise deploy the diary as a means of totalizing and in-dividualizing their ideology?
从内战时期的“红军笔记本”来看，至少有一些革命活动家试图利用日记进行政治教育。这是一本发给每位红军士兵的小册子，他要在其中记录分发给他的弹药、食物和衣服。书末有几页空白。第一页的标题是“个人记事”，随后是这样一条指令：“如果可能，请记下你在工农红军服役期间的日记。”
虽然目前还没有发现任何幸存的笔记本能显示士兵们如何利用分配给个人记事的空间，但这种规定性日记与红军为传授政治素养、使士兵理解自己是具有世界历史意义的斗争参与者而采取的其他策略是一致的。

Judging by the “Red Army notebook” of the civil war period, at least some revolutionary activists sought to make use of the diary for the purposes of political education. This was a booklet handed out to each Red Army soldier, in which he was to record the ammunition, food, and clothing distributed to him. The book contained several blank pages at the end. The first of them bore the heading “For personal notes,” followed by this instruction: “If possible, keep a diary of your service in the Workers’ and Peasants’ Red Army.”

Although no notebooks are known to have survived that would show to what use soldiers put the space allotted for personal notes, this prescriptive diary is in tune with other strategies pursued by the Red Army to impart political literacy and make soldiers comprehend themselves as participants in a struggle of world-historical proportions.

在1917年后的十年里，日记受到了科学家和文学先锋派的特别关注，他们试图将日记文体与革命事业联系起来。其中包括“儿童学家”，即致力于研究儿童的具有革命思想的心理学家。假设年轻人没有自主意识，可以由特定的社会环境塑造，儿童学家相信，研究儿童可以使他们直接了解革命对身心造成的影响。心理学家特别看重日记，因为其所谓的本真性。由于日记是根据作者自己的动议写成的，他们假设它是真诚的，并提供了心理过程未经中介的反映。“分析日记可以让人研究那些在任何其他媒介中都难以揭示的行为形式。”诚然，这种本真性只有在“正确的日记”中才能实现，即被定义为以自我反思模式定期记录的结果。

儿童学家出版年轻人的日记，是为了证明社会环境对个人身心发展的决定性力量。一本最初由维也纳精神分析协会出版的德国女孩日记在1925年出现了俄语译本，由军事医学院的一位教授作序。正如教授所解释的，这本日记描述了一名青春期前女孩的性觉醒，它表明“虚伪的”资产阶级父母和教育者回避“正确的”性教育，让孩子们在压倒性的本能面前束手无策。“这本书应该引起儿童学家、教育家、医生、社会工作者和广大家长的兴趣。它将……迫使许多人反思如何不教育孩子。从这个角度来看，这本书的内容可以用于宣传。”

In the decade after 1917 the diary received attention especially from scientists and the literary avant-garde, who sought to connect the diaristic genre to the revolutionary cause. Among them were “pedologists,” revolutionary-minded psychologists who devoted themselves to the study of the child. Assuming that young people had no autonomous consciousness and could be molded by a given social environment, pedologists believed that examining children yielded direct in-sights into the psycho-physical effects of the revolution. Psychologists valued diaries in particular because of their supposed authenticity. Since a diary was written on the diarist’s own initiative, they assumed that it was sincere and provided an unmediated reflection of psychic processes. “Analyzing a diary allows one to study forms of behavior which are difficult to reveal in any other medium.” To be sure, this authenticity was achieved only in a “correct diary,” which was defined as the result of regular recordkeeping in a self-reflective mode.

Pedologists published young people’s diaries to demonstrate the determining power of the social milieu over an individual’s psycho-physical development. A diary of a German girl, originally published by a Vienna-based psychoanalytical association, appeared in Russian translation in 1925, with a preface by a professor of the Military-Medical Academy. As the professor explained, the diary, which described the sexual awakening of a prepubescent girl, showed that “hypocritical” bourgeois parents and educators shunned “correct” sexual education and left their children helpless in the face of overpowering instincts. “The book should be of interest to pedologists, pedagogues, doctors, social workers, and parents in general. It will . . . force many to reflect on how not to educate children. From this point of view the content of the book can have propagandistic uses.”

1926年《科斯佳·里亚布采夫日记》的出版在某种程度上是苏维埃对德国女孩日记的回应。这是一部由尼古拉·奥格涅夫（M. G. 罗扎诺夫）撰写的虚构日记，它具有如此逼真的感染力，以至于随后出版了两部续集，一位评论者甚至怀疑奥格涅夫是否仅仅是从“真实的”日记中编纂了这些材料。科斯佳是一个叛逆的青少年，淘气且不守纪律，他对虐待儿童、手淫和堕胎等话题的描述比德国女孩的幻想更具体、更令人震惊；然而批评家们将他描绘成苏维埃青年的积极榜样。科斯佳是一个拥有“共产主义信念”的无产者。健全的工人阶级环境保证了他关心社会、积极行动的倾向。虽然科斯佳是个小流氓，但他能区分非无产阶级的胡闹与“无产阶级的胡闹”。在对他生活的描述中，读者绝不会怀疑科斯佳最终会掌控那些导致他无政府主义行为的本能。日记以科斯佳被接纳进入共青团（共产主义青年团组织）而告终。科斯佳的日记（奥格涅夫为此增加了续集）再版多次，无疑在苏维埃读者中普及日记媒介方面发挥了重要作用。1933年，十九岁的工人列昂尼德·波特姆金把自己的日记与科斯佳·里亚布采夫的日记相比，自叹不如，他羡慕科斯佳对生活的实际掌控：“在我的情况下，只有病态的反思。没有实践，没有精彩的公共活动。我必须在实践中掌握生活，我必须生活。”

The publication of the Diary of Kostya Riabtsev in 1926 was in part a Soviet response to the diary of the German girl. A fictional diary, written by Nikolai Ognev (M. G. Rozanov), it had such a lifelike appeal that it was followed by two sequels and one reviewer wondered whether Ognev had not simply compiled the material from “authentic” diaries. Kostya is a rebellious teenager, mischievous and undisciplined, and his account of topics such as child abuse, masturbation, and abortion are more tangible and shocking than the reveries of the German girl; nevertheless critics portrayed him as a positive role model for Soviet youth. Kostya is a proletarian with “Communist convictions.” His sound working-class environment ensures his social and activist disposition. Though a hooligan, Kostya distinguishes between nonproletarian and “proletarian nonsense.” Nowhere in the account of his life does the reader doubt that Kostya will eventually gain control over his instincts, which are responsible for his anarchistic behavior. The diary concludes with Kostya’s acceptance into the Komsomol, the Communist youth organization. Kostya’s diary, to which Ognev added a sequel, went through several editions and undoubtedly played a significant role in popularizing the diary medium among Soviet readers. In 1933 Leonid Potemkin, a nineteen-year-old worker, compared his diary unfavorably to that of Kostya Riabtsev, whom he envied for his practical mastery of life: “In my case there are only sick reflections. No practice, no sparkling public activities. I must master life in practice, I must live.”

儿童学家的抱负超越了利用日记展示社会环境的不利或有利影响。他们寻求创建一个自传写作的语料库，既能证明又能支持无产阶级国家的社会主义方向。1919年，莫斯科儿童学博物馆馆长尼古拉·雷布尼科夫敦促教育人民委员部创建一个传记研究所，致力于收集和分析年轻苏维埃主体的日记和其他自传来源。由于缺乏资金，他的提议落空了，但雷布尼科夫继续向年轻苏维埃公民收集自传证词。到1928年，他已从居住在外省的小学生那里收集了12万份问卷。他的诊断令人清醒：只有一小部分学生知道十年前发生的革命的目的和历史。调查问卷还显示，俄国数量最多的日记作者并非来自儿童学家更愿意在其身上做实验的被剥削阶级，而是来自“资产阶级知识分子”。尽管如此，儿童学家们表示希望，“随着心理文化的增长和对内心世界兴趣的增加，[苏维埃]日记文学有望变得更加广泛。”

有一些迹象表明，早在1920年代，记日记就在苏维埃学校被用作一种教学工具——为了训练语言表达，但也作为一种自我发展的媒介。日记既有个人作业，也有全班作业。一个引人注目的例子是列夫·贝尔恩施坦的日记，他后来成为著名物理学家和科学院院士。他1926年的日记上留有老师用红铅笔修改的痕迹，描述了班级前往沃尔霍夫河大坝的远足，那是苏维埃一系列宏伟建设工程中的第一个：“沃尔霍夫大坝工人新村是苏维埃工人建设的一个美妙成就。这简直是美国！干净、宽阔的街道，两旁是营房：工人的宿舍。每个路口都有一根杆子，上面有照亮的街名和营房编号标牌……沃尔霍夫大坝工人新村是一个示范性的工人公社，它是未来共产主义社会的蓝图。”

Pedologists’ ambitions went beyond using diaries to show the adverse or beneficial influences of the social environment. They sought to create a corpus of autobiographical writing that both testified and lent support to the socialist direction of the proletarian state. In 1919 Nikolai Rybnikov, director of the Moscow Pedological Museum, pressed the People’s Commissariat for Enlightenment to create a biographical institute, to be devoted to the collection and analysis of diaries and other autobiographical sources by young Soviet subjects. His initiative fell through for lack of funding, but Rybnikov proceeded to collect autobiographical testimony from young Soviet citizens. By 1928 he had collected 120,000 questionnaires from grade-school students living in the provinces. His diagnosis was sobering: only a small fraction of these students knew the purpose and the history of the revolution, which had taken place ten years before. The questionnaires also revealed that the greatest number of diarists in Russia hailed not from the exploited classes, with whom the pedological profession preferred to experiment, but from the “bourgeois intelligentsia.” Nevertheless pedologists expressed hope that “with the growth of psychological culture and the increase of interest in the inner world, [Soviet] diary literature can be expected to become much more widespread.”

There are a few indications that as early as the 1920s diary-writing was used in Soviet schools as a pedagogical tool—to train linguistic expression, but also as a medium of self-development. Diaries were assigned both on an individual level and for the class as a whole. A striking example is the diary of Lev Bernshtein, a teenager who would later become a well-known physicist and member of the Academy of Sciences. His diary of 1926, which bears traces of the teacher’s correcting red pencil, describes a class excursion to the Volkhov River dam, the first in a series of grand Soviet construction projects: “The Volkhov dam workers’ settlement is a wonderful achievement of Soviet workers’ construction. It’s a real America! Clean, large streets, with barracks on both sides: dormitories for the workers. At each intersection there is a pole with illuminated signs of the street name and the barracks numbers . . . The Volkhov dam workers’ settlement is an exemplary workers’ commune, it is a blueprint for Communist society of the future.”

贝尔恩施坦的日记还展示了学生获取并内化苏维埃的政治与社会学分类体系的机制。在参观大坝附近的旧拉多加地区时，他们领到的“任务”是结识“不同类型的农民”，“我们在他们身上试图发现社会分化的迹象，尽管后者在村庄中并未明显地显露自身。”他们被要求区分受剥削的贫农、中农，以及剥削他人的富农，即不祥的“富农”（库拉克）。讽刺的是，正是那个富农最让学生们着迷，他讲述了在农奴制下和革命降临后的生活，“当时我们的兄弟，工人和农民，统治着我们的祖国俄罗斯。”贝尔恩施坦的老师对他对这位农民剥削者的钦佩描述未加评论——这证明了1920年代被广泛视为一个意识形态受污染的时代，在那个时代，人们可以发表一些在1930年代历史更发达的社会主义环境中必然会被解读为异端且对共产主义意识形态具有危险破坏性的言论。

Bernshtein’s diary also demonstrates the mechanisms through which pupils were to acquire and internalize Soviet political and sociological taxonomy. Visiting the Old Ladoga region near the dam, they were assigned the “task” of making the acquaintance of “different types of peasants, in whom we try to detect signs of social differentiation, although the latter have not actively revealed themselves in the village.” They were to distinguish between exploited, poor; middle; and exploiting, rich peasants, the ominous kulaks. Ironically it was a kulak who most fascinated the students with his accounts of life under serfdom and the advent of the revolution, “when our brothers, the worker and the peasant, governed our Mother Russia.” Bernshtein’s teacher left his admiring characterization of this peasant-exploiter uncommented upon—a testimony to how widely the 1920s were regarded as an ideologically contaminated age in which it was legitimate to make statements that in the historically more developed socialist environment of the 1930s were bound to be read as heretical and dangerously subversive of Communist ideology.

日记的重要性也受到了“左翼艺术阵线”（LEF）的强调，这是一个由苏维埃先锋派作家组成的团体，旨在创造无产阶级文化。LEF 的具体目标是推广一种新的文学风格，称为“事实文学”。这些活动家为新文学辩护，理由是：以资产阶级小说为典型代表的传统文学风格已经过时。小说的主要特征在于它脱离当下生活的关切与实践；它的作用只是迷惑读者，作用于他的想象。相比之下，“我们的史诗是报纸……谈论书本上的小说有什么好处……当我们每天早晨抓起报纸，就翻开了那部名为《我们的今天》的最令人震惊的小说的新一页。这部小说中的人物、作者和读者，就是我们自己。”
LEF 所倡导的文学是记录性的，或实录性的，涵盖各种见证苏维埃国家革命议程的资料。这些大部分是人的文件：传记、回忆录、游记、自传和日记。将这些文本维系在一起的是“事实”，它作为“建造大厦的主要材料细胞”。与资产阶级文学的沉思唯心主义形成对比，这是一种“新的美学……或者更确切地说是一门新科学……新的艺术科学以通过改造现实来改变现实为前提……因此强调文献，因此强调事实文学。”
隐含地，LEF 鼓励每一位无产者记一份日记，记录苏维埃生活各个领域正在进行的史诗般的改造和自我改造过程。日记的日历网格有助于LEF 逐日记录建设未来的议程。然而，只有当苏维埃生活在社会和个人心理层面的“事实”随着时间的推移展现出稳定的发展时，这一议程才成立。

The significance of diary-keeping was also emphasized by the “Left Front in Art” (LEF), a group of Soviet avant-garde writers associated for the purpose of creating a proletarian culture. The particular goal of LEF was to promote a new literary style, called “literature of the fact.” These activists grounded their call for a new literature in the claim that the traditional literary style, epitomized in the bourgeois novel, had become outdated. The novel was characterized chiefly by its detachment from the concerns and practices of current life; its effect was only to mystify the reader, to work on his imagination. By contrast, “Our epics are the newspapers . . . What is the good of talking about bookish novels . . . when every morning as we snatch our newspaper we turn over a new page of the most astounding novel called Our Today. The characters in this novel, its authors, and its readers, are we ourselves.”

The literature advocated by LEF was documentary, or factographic, encompassing a wide variety of sources which testified to the revolutionary agenda of the Soviet state. These were for the most part human documents: biographies, memoirs, travelogues, autobiographies, and diaries. Holding these texts together was the “fact,” which acted as the “primary material cell for the construction of the edifice.” In contrast to the contemplative idealism of bourgeois literature, this was a “new aesthetic . . . or rather a new science . . . The new science of art presupposes to change reality by transforming it . . . Hence the emphasis on the document, and hence literature of the fact.”

Implicitly, LEF encouraged every proletarian to keep a daily diary that would document the epic process of transformation and self-transformation under way in all areas of Soviet life. The calendar grid of the diary lent itself to LEF’s agenda of documenting the building of the future, day by day. Yet this agenda worked only if the “facts” of Soviet life, on both social and individual psychic levels, revealed a steady development over time.

就共产党人对日记的看法而言，值得注意的是，关于这一时期记日记最广泛的讨论发生在莫斯科地铁的施工现场。莫斯科地铁在高尔基的“工厂史”项目中占据了核心地位。与作为该项目组成部分的所有其他工厂和建筑工地一样，地铁建设局（Metrostroy）成立了一个由专业作家组成的编辑委员会；他们的任务是指导工人回忆录的创作，并最终将它们出版在装帧精美的纪实丛书中。地铁建设局的编辑们特别鼓励工人写“生产日记”，其中最优秀的将被列入规划中的卷册。编辑们的讨论阐明了他们所构想的苏联日记写作的形式和目标——无论是在建筑工地还是在其他地方。一方面，日记被视为劳动过程中的一种惩戒技术；它旨在鼓励工人作者“保持更多的秩序，更加系统化，反思自己的所作所为，以便吸收并强化他的[工作]经验”。正如一位编辑利奥波德·阿维尔巴赫（Leopold Averbakh）所言，记日记应当像党的“清洗”一样进行：“你在每一件事上审视自己，做了什么，怎么做的。写日记必须让工人或其他人问自己，他在特定的一天里做了什么有价值的事情。”

编辑们认为日记诱导自我反思的能力是一个关键方面：“日记……是日复一日盘点自己行为的方式；是反思一个人的生活。”工人日记不应仅仅是一份工作记录，而应“展示整个人发展的过程”。最终，编辑们希望日记作者将他们的生活与建筑工地联系起来，并理解他们的主观生活是在建设社会主义的框架内演进的。这一过程既是总体化的（就向集体开放自我而言），又是自我完成的（在发挥个人创造力的意义上）。一方面，“每一个[个人的]传记[都将]成为地铁传记的一部分”。另一方面，专门报道建筑工地的出版物被期望有助于塑造每个撰稿人的个性。“集体创作”的行为旨在“丰富每个创作者的个性”。
在审议苏联生产日记时，编辑们力求使其不同于“资产阶级”日记——那种充满了徒劳谈话的社会无用记录。其中一人利奥波德·阿维尔巴赫问道：“为什么我们经常看不起日记？”“因为日记意味着女高中生的活动：一个坐下来写各种废话的女孩。”相比之下，阿维尔巴赫强调，苏联生产日记牢牢扎根于专注的、集体的奋斗环境中，这赋予了它方向和用途：“在我们这里，日记是整个体系的一部分。”
除了让日记作者与苏联项目保持一致外，写日记还有公共目的。日记和回忆录将在工人班组中讨论，并印在墙报上，以教育和动员集体中落后的成员。因此，编辑们坚持要求尤其是“突击队员”（即超过劳动定额的工人）写日记。他们卓越的工作记录显示了他们成熟的政治意识，并让人希望他们能写出特别适合收录在纪念地铁建设出版物中的日记。突击队员还要鼓励其他能力较弱的工人记日记并对自己进行修炼。
苏联生产日记，正如其发起人所构想的那样，既是一份披露个人精神本质的强烈个人化文件，又是一份公共的教育文本；就像清教徒日记一样，它将精神功能与宣传功能结合在一起。编辑们从未将生产日记——或整个日记体裁——视为纯粹的私人文件。相反，它是自我形成的媒介和工具，根据个人与集体、主观与客观的融合来定义。

Tellingly for Communist conceptions of the diary, it was at the construction site of the Moscow metro where the most wide-ranging discussion on diary-keeping during this period took place. The Moscow metro occupied a central place in Gorky’s “History of the Factories” project. As with all the other factories and construction sites that formed part of this project, an editorial board of professional writers was instituted at Metrostroy; their task was to direct the production of workers’ memoirs and eventually publish them in lavish documentary series. The Metrostroy editors specifically encouraged workers to write “production diaries,” the best of which were to be included in the projected volumes. The deliberations among the editors shed light on what they envisioned as the forms and goals of Soviet diary-keeping— on the construction site and beyond. For one, the diary figured as a disciplining technique in the labor process; it was to encourage the worker-author to “keep more order, to be more systematic, to reflect about what he does, in order to assimilate and reinforce his [work] experience.” As one editor, Leopold Averbakh, put it, diary-keeping was to proceed like a party “purge”: “You examine yourself in everything, what and how. The diary must we written so that the worker or another person asks himself what he has done of value on a given day.”

The editors considered the ability of the diary to induce self-re-flection as a key aspect: “The diary . . . is a way of establishing the balance of one’s actions, day after day; of reflecting on one’s life.” More than a mere work record, the worker’s journal should “show the process of development of the entire person.” Ultimately, the editors wanted diarists to link their lives to the construction site, and to understand that their subjective lives evolved within the frame of the construction of socialism. This process was to be both totalizing, in terms of opening the self to the collective, and self-completing, in the sense of bringing out the individual’s creative faculties. On one hand, “every [individual] biography [was] to become a part of the biography of the metro.” On the other, the publication devoted to the construction site was expected to contribute to the shaping of the personality of each contributor. The act of “collective creation” was to “enrich each creator’s individuality.”

In deliberating about the Soviet production diary, the editors sought to make it unlike a “bourgeois” diary—a socially useless record filled with ineffectual talk: “Why do we often look down on the diary?” one of them, Leopold Averbakh, asked. “Because the diary connotes a girl’s high school activity: a girl who sits down and writes all sorts of nonsense.” By contrast, Averbakh emphasized, the Soviet production diary was firmly embedded in an environment of concentrated, collective striving which lent it direction and use: “In our case, the diary is part of a system.”

Beyond aligning the diarist to the Soviet project, diary-writing also had a public purpose. Diaries and memoirs were to be discussed in worker brigades and printed on wall newspapers to educate and mobilize lagging members of the collective. Hence the editors’ insistence that especially “shock workers,” workers who exceeded their labor norms, write diaries. Their exceptional work records pointed to their developed political consciousness and lent hope that they would produce diaries particularly suitable for inclusion in the published volumes commemorating the building of the metro. The shock workers were also to encourage other, less able workers to keep diaries and to work on themselves.

The Soviet production diary, as envisioned by its progenitors, was at once an intensely personal document, disclosing the individual’s spiritual essence, and a public, educational text; much like the Puritan diary, it welded spiritual to propagandistic functions. The editors never conceived of the production diary—or of the diary genre as a whole—as a purely private document. Rather, it was a medium and tool of self-formation, defined in terms of the merging of the individual and the collective, the subjective and the objective.

假设工人不熟悉日记体裁，不知道如何写“创造性日记”，编辑委员会制定了关于如何“正确”撰写生产日记的详细指南。他们列出了日记作者在反思中应当涉及的一系列问题：“党及其领导作用；……工程师的作用；共青团的面貌；国际生活；地铁建设局内部的阶级斗争；妇女与地铁；文化与生活方式；全莫斯科都在建地铁，全[苏联]都在建地铁。”这些规定以呼吁真实表达达到高潮：“日记的基本要求是最大限度的真实、诚恳和可靠。不要伪文学……写出真相！”真相将通过忠实地遵守编辑提供的风格和主题指南来获得。它被定义为日记作者对政治生活的正确理解，以及他在政治生活展开过程中定位自己的能力，无论是“地铁建设局的阶级斗争”还是“国际生活”。真理只能作为一种内在体验被感受到，它超越了外在表现的表象，而产生真理的场所正是日记：“日记是我们对世界的意识的反映。人必须超越表象，超越眼球捕捉到的东西。人必须理解事件，并在事件之间建立联系。必须有一个中心主题。日记的标准是真实。”编辑们强调，真实的表现不应导致对现实的美化。记录生活中的负面现象不仅是允许的，而且是必要的。然而，日记作者还必须解释这些缺陷的来源和性质。

这项倡议的结果证明令人失望。只有一小部分地铁工人响应了写日记的号召。在编辑收到的日记中，许多写得很不通顺，充满拼写错误和拙劣的表达。其他的则没有达到编辑力求达到的解释深度，反而证实了他们最初的担忧，即生产日记会被当作纯粹的“账本”，详细记录某一天“完成了多少立方米”。叙述是“肤浅的”和“干燥的”，缺乏“内在性”，没有“触及本质的东西”。最糟糕的是，它们运行在“无用”的描述或沉思层面，从而未能通过“正确”日记的测试，而正确的日记“必须为行动而构思”。地铁建设局集体自传记录的宏伟计划没有结出预期的果实。
最终，编辑委员会出版了两卷与莫斯科地铁建设相关的回忆录和自传草图——但不是日记。

编辑们不得不承认，他们原本“极为重视”的征集生产日记计划，需要比预期长得多的时间。尽管如此，他们并没有失去对日记媒介意义的信心。正如其中一位编辑所评论的：“我们必须记日记吗？毫无疑问。它们可以产生伟大的结果，但这些结果不会在一夜之间到来。日记需要时间，但我们现在就需要材料。”这最后一句话说明了一种显而易见的犹豫。编辑们相信，在遥远的未来，具有成熟政治意识的社会主义公民将写出他们所呼吁的那种日记。然而，在目前，如果没有广泛的编辑监督和干预，这样的日志是无法产生的。由于急于记录苏联政权进行的历史性变革，编辑们转向了工人的回忆录，与日记相比，回忆录的制作速度更快，更容易监督，并能产生传记性的结果。

Assuming that workers were not familiar with the diaristic genre and would not know how to keep a “creative diary,” the editorial board established detailed guidelines on how to “correctly” write a production diary. They outlined a number of questions that the diarist should engage as part of his reflections: “The party, its guiding role; . . . the role of the engineer; the face of the Komsomol; international life; class struggle in the Metrostroy; women and the metro; culture and way of life; all of Moscow builds the metro, all of the [Soviet] Union builds the metro.” These prescriptions culminated with a call for truthful representation: “The essential exigency of the diary is maximum truth, sincerity, and authenticity. No pseudo-literature . . . Write the truth!” Truth was to be attained through a faithful adherence to the stylistic and thematic guidelines provided by the editors. It was defined as a diarist’s correct understanding of political life and his ability to position himself in its unfolding, be it “the class struggle in the Metrostroy” or “international life.” Truth could be felt only as an inner experience, transcending the veneer of external appearances, and the site at which it was to be produced was the diary: “The diary is the reflection of our consciousness of the world. One must go beyond appearances, beyond what captures the eye. One has to understand events, create links between them. There must be a central theme. The criterion of the diary is truth.” Truthful representation, the editors stressed, should not lead to an embellishment of reality. It was not only permissible but necessary for the diarist to record negative appearances in life. Yet he also had to explain the provenance and nature of these deficiencies.

The results of the initiative proved disappointing. Only a fraction of the metro workers heeded the appeal to write diaries. Of the journals the editors received, many were barely literate, filled with orthographic errors and clumsy expressions. Others did not reach the inter-pretive depth the editors had sought to attain, instead confirming their initial fears that production diaries would be kept as mere “account books,” detailing “how many cubic meters were done” on a given day. The narratives were “superficial” and “dry,” they lacked “interiority,” they did not “get to essential things.” Worst of all, they operated on the “useless” level of description or contemplation, thus failing the test of the “correct” diary, which “must be conceived for action.” The grand project of a collective autobiographical record of the Metrostroy did not bear its intended fruit.
Eventually the editorial commission published two volumes with memoirs and autobiographical sketches—but not diaries—related to the building of the Moscow metro.

The editors had to concede that their plan to elicit production diaries, to which they had attached “very great importance,” was a much longer-term endeavor than they had anticipated. Still, they had not lost faith in the significance of the diary medium. As one of the editors re-marked: “Do we have to keep diaries? Without any doubt. They can give great results, but these results won’t come overnight. The diary demands time, but we need material now.” This final statement bespeaks a revealing hesitation. In some distant future, the editors believed, socialist citizens with developed political consciousness would write the type of diaries they had called for. At present, however, such journals could not be produced without extensive editorial supervision and intervention. Impatient to document the historical transformation carried out by the Soviet regime, the editors turned to workers’ memoirs, which, compared with diaries, were more quickly produced, more easily supervised, and yielded biographical results.
如果说一般的苏联工人仍然缺乏足够的政治素养来记一份“正确”的日记，那么像德米特里·富尔曼诺夫这样政治意识毋庸置疑的共产党人又如何呢？富尔曼诺夫和其他激进知识分子成员一样，是一位坚持不懈的日记作者。

但即使对他来说，记日记也是一件有争议的事情。他反复担心，在日记中写作会导致他过度强调个人生活的各个方面，从而使他与革命和苏联人民的命运脱节。由于强调个人情感，强调“爱、痛苦、幸福、记忆、期望”，他的日记让他想起了尼古拉二世的日记，他记得在1917年的报纸上读过其中的摘录：“我吃饭，在花园里散步，躺在草地上，亲爱的太阳照耀着，我吵了一架——等等等等。”但是，富尔曼诺夫急忙补充道，他与末代罗曼诺夫的根本区别在于，他的大部分生命都致力于“革命”的伟大事业——这是他的日记未能传达的一种承诺。富尔曼诺夫确信，日记媒介无法捕捉到他生命的全部本质。
这种抒情的个人领域与史诗般的“生活”之间的冲突，在富尔曼诺夫的文学英雄费奥多尔·克雷奇科夫（Fedor Klychkov）的日记中并不存在。克雷奇科夫的日记浑然一体——它体现了一种成熟理性的声音，坚定地致力于社会用途和革命行动。因此，克雷奇科夫的记录代表了富尔曼诺夫心目中理想的共产主义日记。

If Soviet workers in general still lacked sufficient political literacy to keep a “correct” diary, what about Communists like Dmitri Furmanov, whose political consciousness was beyond doubt? Furmanov, along with other members of the radical intelligentsia, was a dedicated diarist.

But even for him, keeping a journal was a controversial matter. He repeatedly worried that writing in the diary led him to overemphasize aspects of his personal life, thus disconnecting him from the revolution and the fate of the Soviet people. With its emphasis on personal emotions, on “love, suffering, happiness, memories, expectations,” his diary made him think of the diary of Nicholas II, excerpts of which he remembered reading in a 1917 newspaper: “I ate, took a walk in the garden, lay on the grass, the dear sun was shining, I had a quarrel—etc. etc.” But, Furmanov hastened to add, what distinguished him fundamentally from the last Romanov was that the bulk of his life was devoted to the great cause of “the Revolution”—a commitment that his diary failed to convey. Furmanov was convinced that the diary medium could not capture the full essence of his life.

This conflict between a lyrical personal realm and an epic “life” is not present in the diary of Furmanov’s literary hero, Fedor Klychkov. Klychkov’s diary is of one mold—it bespeaks a voice of developed reason, firmly dedicated to social use and revolutionary action. As such, Klychkov’s record stood for what Furmanov imagined to be the ideal Communist diary.

即使在20世纪30年代初，当共产党人开始称颂新社会主义个人“丰富的个人生活”时，他们仍对日记有所保留。在苏联环境下，日记是否是自我训练和个人化的合适工具，仍然是一个值得怀疑的问题。30年代中期，一名共青团活动家斥责一位朋友，因为后者建议“一个人通过日记，通过组织和研究自我，来寻找自己发展的道路”：“不，亲爱的，人一生中最宝贵的是他的工作，而不是他的日记……因为了解并热爱自己的工作，……与数百万成员的集体保持步调一致，是当代训练和自我训练的主要内容。日记不是一种自我训练的方法，而是一种自我挖掘的方法。它适用于那些‘知识分子’（在这个词的贬义意义上），他们‘研究’自己，挖掘自己心理的深度——瞧，我是一个卑鄙、软弱的人；瞧，我干了什么错事。”

虽然共青团活动家与其通信者一致认为，共产党人应当“组织”自己的精神生活，使其与集体的生活保持一致，但他批评日记是一种无用甚至有害的工具。作为一种纯粹的反思媒介，它带有使思想脱离行动、精神脱离身体、个人脱离集体的风险。个人记日记的行为本身就可能削弱共产党人的本质——他的意志力，而意志力需要靠近集体和工作领域才能得到补充。因此，日记似乎有一种令人不安的能力，能将独自写作的共产党人变成资产阶级主体。共产党人的强壮与资产阶级的软弱之间的对比，也在所谓男性特质——坚定、理性、集体行动——与女性特质——自恋、歇斯底里、对社会无用的闲谈——之间构成了对立。后一类特征有时被认定为是日记作为一种文学形式的特征。由于被认为有使共产党人资产阶级化、软弱化、女性化的倾向，日记在整个30年代苏联政权推广的众多“自我修炼”形式中并不突出。

Communists continued to express reservations about the diary, even as they began to evoke the “rich personal life” of the new socialist individual in the early 1930s. It remained a matter of doubt whether the diary was a suitable tool for self-training and individualization in a Soviet setting. A Komsomol activist in the mid-1930s rebuked a friend for suggesting “that a man works out the way of his own development by means of a diary, by means of organizing and studying his own self”: “No, my dear, what is most valuable in man’s life is his work and not his diary . . . Because knowing and loving one’s work, . . . keeping in step with the multimillion-member collective, is the main thing in contemporary training and self-training. And the diary is not a method of self-training, but a method of self-rummaging. It is suitable for the ‘in-tellectuals’ (in the derogatory sense of the word) who ‘study’ themselves and dig in the depths of their own psychology—here am I, a mean and weak-willed man; here is the misdeed I committed.”

While in agreement with his correspondent that a Communist should “organize” his psychic life so as to align it with the life of the collective, the Komsomol activist criticized the diary as a useless and, indeed, harmful instrument. A purely reflective medium, it carried the risk of divorcing thought from action, the mind from the body, and the individual from the collective. The very act of individual diary-keeping could weaken the Communist’s essence—his willpower, which needed the proximity of the collective and the work sphere to be re-plenished. Thus the diary had the uncanny ability to remake solitary, writing Communists into bourgeois subjects. The contrast between Communist strength and bourgeois weakness evoked an opposition as well between supposedly male attributes of firm, rational, and collective action and female narcissism, hysteria, and socially useless chatter. These last characteristics were sometimes identified with the diary as a literary form. Tainted by its supposed proclivity to make the Communist bourgeois, weak, feminine, the diary did not figure prominently among the many forms of “work on the self” that the Communist regime promoted throughout the 1930s.

从20世纪20年代到30年代的转变，意味着从一个妥协和历史不纯的时代，过渡到一个不妥协地追求极度纯洁的最终历史时代。这种转变影响了苏维埃领域日记的读者群以及阅读风格。20世纪20年代最著名的日记读者和分析家是儿童学家，他们将日志中意识的偏差追溯到不完美的苏联现状的社会环境。1936年，儿童学专业被废除，当时苏联社会宣布所有阶级对立都已被消灭。现在，内务人民委员部（NKVD）成了苏联日记的主要解读机构。

内务人民委员部官员分析了搜查疑似反革命分子住所时缴获的日记，寻找主观上背离或反对苏联政权所体现的单一社会主义历史形态的迹象。内务人民委员部官员并没有接受过心理学家或文学专家的培训，但他们完全认同儿童学家和苏联写作界所持有的假设，即日记披露了作者的真相——无论是日记内容的直接表达，还是其直接反转。在后一种情况下，内务人民委员部假设反革命敌人伪装成共产党人，而他们忠诚的共产主义日记构成了精心设计的伪装的一部分。

The turn from the 1920s to the 1930s entailed a transition from an age of compromise and historical impurity to the uncompromising pursuit of a final historical age of utmost purity. This transition affected the readership as well as the reading styles of diaries in the Soviet realm. The most prominent readers and analysts of diaries during the 1920s were pedologists, who traced lapses in consciousness in a journal back to the social environment of the imperfect Soviet present. The pedological profession was abolished in 1936, when all class antagonisms were decreed to have been abolished in Soviet society. Now the NKVD became the chief interpreting agency of Soviet diaries.

NKVD officers analyzed diaries seized during searches of the apartments of suspected counterrevolutionaries for signs of subjective deviation from, or opposition to, the single, socialist historical formation that the Soviet regime embodied. NKVD officials were not trained as psychologists or literary experts, but they fully shared the assumption held both by pedologists and the Soviet writing profession that the diary disclosed the truth about its author—whether in direct expression of what the lines said or in its direct inversion. In the latter case the NKVD assumed that counterrevolutionary enemies were masquerading as Communists and that their loyal Communist diaries formed part of the elaborate mask.

在两个著名的案例中，被控反革命罪的共产党人的日记被公开引用，以揭露他们的道德和政治面貌。第一个案例涉及鲍里斯·科泽列夫（Boris Kozelev），他是一位工会领导人，也是米哈伊尔·托姆斯基（Mikhail Tomsky）的支持者，托姆斯基在20世纪20年代后期被斥为“右倾分子”而名誉扫地。科泽列夫在日记中讽刺地评论了斯大林如何逐一击败对手，并巩固了对自己作为政治领袖的个人崇拜。发现日记的是一名醉酒同事；科泽列夫曾把他带回家，让他在自己的办公室里醒酒。同事在科泽列夫办公桌的抽屉里发现了日记，并将其交给国家政治保卫局（GPU，1934年更名为NKVD
），后者将其转交给政治局。日记的段落出现在苏联报刊上，报刊谴责作者的“反党恶作剧”。1930年6月的第十六次党代表会议
也讨论了这份日记，在那次会议上，右翼反对派的命运被最终确定。科泽列夫被开除出共产党，他似乎至少接受了部分指控：作为赎罪的姿态，他开始在莫斯科的“锤子与镰刀”工厂担任金属工人，并于1930年秋前往马格尼托哥尔斯克协助建设这座钢铁之城。他于1936年被捕，1937年被处决。

另一份受到共产党领导人和内务人民委员部严密审查的日记是列昂尼德·尼古拉耶夫（Leonid Nikolaev）的，他是一名心怀不满的共产党人，于1934年12月枪杀了谢尔盖·基洛夫，并引发了斯大林针对其昔日对手（包括托姆斯基和科泽列夫）的政治恐怖运动。尼古拉耶夫被捕时，在他的公文包里发现了他的日记。这份日记在谋杀案调查报告中被显著引用，成为一名共产党人内心堕落、最终杀害同志的主要证据。尼古拉耶夫在日记中描述了他在1934年初受到共产党申斥后的沮丧心情，以及他的挫败感如何演变成一种有意识的决定：攻击那个曾将他逐出的集体。
无论是在尼古拉耶夫还是在科泽列夫的案例中，检察官都没有争辩说嫌疑人写日记这一事实本身就构成了犯罪。相反，他们关注的是日记揭示了作者的什么信息。虽然共产主义观察者可能会在秘密的个人记日记习惯与它可能诱发的主观退化状态之间建立因果联系，但这种论点并未被提出。这进一步表明，日记在共产主义想象中的地位是多么不一致，它时而被塑造成自我完善的合法媒介，时而又被说成一种固有的资产阶级追求。

In two prominent cases, diaries of Communists accused of counterrevolutionary crimes were publicly cited to disclose their moral and political makeup. The first of them involved Boris Kozelev, a trade union leader and a supporter of Mikhail Tomsky, who was discredited in the late 1920s as a “Right Deviationist.” In his diary Kozelev sarcastically commented on the way Stalin outmaneuvered his adversaries one by one and consolidated the cult of himself as political leader. The diary was discovered by a drunken colleague whom Kozelev had brought home and put up in his office to sober up. The colleague found the diary in a drawer of Kozelev’s desk and passed it on to the GPU (the Soviet secret police, renamed NKVD in 1934), which forwarded it to the Politburo. Passages from the diary appeared in the Soviet press, which denounced the author for his “anti-party pranks.” The diary was also discussed at the Sixteenth Party Conference in June 1930, at which the fate of the Right Opposition was sealed. Kozelev, who was expelled from the Communist party, seemed to accept at least some of the charges: in a gesture of expiation he set out to work as a metal worker in Moscow’s “Hammer and Sickle” plant, and in the fall of 1930 he left for Magnitogorsk to help build the city of steel. He was arrested in 1936 and shot in 1937.

Another diary intensely scrutinized by Communist leaders and the NKVD was that of Leonid Nikolaev, the disaffected Communist who shot Sergei Kirov in December 1934 and set off Stalin’s political terror campaign against his erstwhile adversaries, including Tomsky and Kozelev. When Nikolaev was arrested, his diary was found in his briefcase. The diary, prominently cited in reports of the murder investigation, served as prime evidence of the process of inner degeneration that had led a Communist to kill a comrade. In his diary Nikolaev described his despondency after being reprimanded by the Communist party in early 1934, and how his frustration turned into a conscious decision to attack the collective body from which he had been expelled.

Neither in Nikolaev’s nor in Kozelev’s case did prosecutors argue that the very fact that the suspect wrote a diary incriminated him. Instead they focused on what the diaries revealed about their authors. While a Communist observer might have established a causal link between secretive individual diary-keeping and the state of subjective degeneration that it possibly induced, this argument was not made. This was a further indication of how inconsistently the diary fared in the Communist imagination, cast alternatively as a legitimate medium of self-perfection and as an inherently bourgeois pursuit.

尽管布尔什维克革命与十七世纪的清教主义都具有自我激活的特质和个性化的冲动，但这两场运动追求的目标却不尽相同。清教徒极其看重基督信徒与其灵魂的关系。从定义上讲，堕落之人的灵魂是有罪的，但通过警惕的自我观察来承认并暴露自己的罪孽，是信徒在来世获得救赎的关键。日记的日历网格和第一人称叙事赋予了它作为每日记录的力量，罪孽深重的基督徒在其中设立了个人良心法庭。作为一种每日的自我参与形式，日记实践是救赎工作的基本组成部分；因此，清教徒赋予日记作为自我实践和宣传工具的核心意义。相比之下，布尔什维克革命并非导向来世；它致力于改变这个世界。因此，苏联共产党人力求灌输一种普遍意识，以促使公民采取自觉行动。与清教徒关注作为目标本身的内在性不同，苏联文化将自觉的外在活动视为最高价值。自觉行动的前提是自我认知和自我掌控，以及有序的身心生活。就此而言，内在性也很重要，但它仅仅是通往自觉劳动行为的踏脚石。

In spite of the ethos of self-activation and the individuating thrust that characterized the Bolshevik revolution as well as seventeenth-century Puritanism, the two movements pursued different goals. The Puritans accorded the utmost importance to a Christian believer’s relationship with his soul. By definition the soul of a fallen man was sinful, but to acknowledge and expose one’s sin through vigilant self-observation was key to the believer’s salvation in the afterlife. The diary’s calendar grid and first-person narrative lent it power as a daily record in which the sinful Christian staged a personal court of conscience. As a daily form of self-engagement, diaristic practice was the essential component of the work of salvation; hence the central significance Puritans accorded to the diary both as a self-practice and as a propagandistic tool. The Bolshevik revolution, by contrast, was not oriented toward an afterworld; it was bent on changing this world. Hence Soviet Communists sought to instill a universal consciousness in order to propel citizens into conscious action. In contrast to the Puritans’ concern with interiority as a goal in and of itself, Soviet culture accorded the highest value to conscious external activity. To act consciously presupposed self-knowledge and self-mastery, an ordered psycho-physical life. To this extent, interiority was important, too, but only as a stepping stone toward the act of conscious labor.

意识与行动作为衡量个人在苏维埃领域价值的尺度，也是评判记日记价值的决定性标准。如果日记作者利用日记来强化自己在苏联集体内工作的精神投入，那么记日记就是一项合法且有价值的追求。可以说，地铁建设局编辑构思的生产日记是理想的苏联日记：其目的是培养对工作场所的日记式反思，从而将体力劳动与精神奉献结合起来。工作环境和劳动集体，加上编辑委员会的指导，将确保日记作者的思想安全地朝着有意识的行动方向前进。然而，要以这种方式运作，生产日记需要具备政治素养的日记作者，而在莫斯科地铁施工现场，这类人并不多见。至于那些在工作领域和集体监控目光之外撰写的日记，则带有削弱而非增强作者共产主义意志的风险。它们有可能使反思以牺牲行动为代价取得优先地位，因此被以矛盾和某种程度的怀疑态度看待。这些顾虑有助于解释为什么日记在布尔什维克国家执行的主体化政策中不具有核心意义。

Consciousness and action as the measure of an individual’s worth in the Soviet realm were also the decisive criteria against which the value of diary-keeping was judged. To keep a diary was a legitimate and valuable pursuit if the diarist used it to reinforce his mental commitment toward work within the Soviet collective. Arguably the production diary envisioned by the Metrostroy editors was the ideal Soviet diary: its purpose was to foster diaristic reflection on the work space and thus imbricate physical work with mental dedication. The environment of work and the laboring collective, combined with guidance by the editorial board, would make sure that the diarist’s thoughts traveled safely in the direction of conscious action. Yet to operate in this fashion, the production diary required politically literate diarists, who were not to be found in significant numbers at the Moscow metro construction site. As for diaries that were written outside the work sphere and the monitoring gaze of the collective, they carried the risk of diminishing rather than enhancing their authors’ Communist will. They threatened to privilege reflection at the expense of action, and were therefore looked upon with ambivalence and a degree of suspicion. These reservations help explain why diaries were not of central significance for the subjectivization policies carried out by the Bolshevik state.
因此，苏联日记作者在缺乏清教徒日记那种规范文化的情况下书写他们的个人记录。他们不确定记日记的好处，也不确定如何记一份“正确”的日记。他们中的大多数人是主动写日记的，有些人的确感叹缺乏关于如何实现自我转型工作的官方准则。因此，研究这些日记可以看出，个人在自行行动时，在多大程度上创造性地将自己编织进苏联革命产生的松散主体化框架，以及他们自己如何提供了苏联式自我实现的一些核心范畴与机制。

Thus Soviet diarists wrote their personal records in the absence of the prescriptive culture that characterized the Puritan diary. They were unsure about the benefits of diary-keeping and of how to keep a “correct” diary. Most of them wrote diaries on their own initiative, and some in fact lamented the absence of official precepts for how to achieve the work of self-transformation. An investigation of these diaries thus highlights the extent to which individuals, acting on their own, creatively wove themselves into a loose matrix of subjectivization produced by the Soviet Revolution, and how these individuals themselves supplied some of the core categories and mechanisms of self-re-alization in a Soviet vein.

V. 朱拉夫廖夫（S. V. Zhuravlev）著，《〈工厂史〉现象：1930年代背景下的高尔基倡议》（Fenomen “Istorii fabrik i zavodov”: Gor’kovskoe nachinanie v kontekste epokhi 1930-kh godov）（莫斯科：俄罗斯科学院俄罗斯历史研究所，1997年）。
en:
Josette Bouvard, “Le moi au miroir de la société nouvelle: les formes
autobiographiques de l’histoire” (manuscript), 61–62; see also Josette
Bouvard, “Une fabrique d’écriture, le projet de Gorki L’Histoire des
fabriques et des usines (1931–1936),” in Autobiographies, autocritiques, aveux
dans le monde communiste, ed. Claude Pennetier and Bernard Pudal
(Paris: Belin, 2002), 63–83. S. V. Zhuravlev, Fenomen “Istorii fabrik i
zavodov”: Gor’kovskoe nachinanie v kontekste epokhi 1930-kh godov (Mos-
cow: In-tut rossiiskoi istoriii RAN, 1997).

zh: 布瓦尔著，《新社会镜子里的自我》，第64–65、68、89页。
en: Bouvard, “Le moi au miroir,” 64–65, 68, 89.

zh: 同上，第62页。
en: Ibid., 62.

zh: 《地铁建设者的故事》（Rasskazy stroitelei metro）（莫斯科，1935年）；《我们是如何建设地铁的》（Kak my stroili metro）（莫斯科：工厂史出版社，1935年）。
en:
Rasskazy stroitelei metro (Moscow, 1935); Kak my stroili metro (Moscow:
“Istoriia fabrik i zavodov,” 1935).

zh: 布瓦尔著，《新社会镜子里的自我》，第85页。那个时代的一篇百科全书文章赞扬了回忆录“通过特定意识形态概念的棱镜”组织作者生活的能力，并轻蔑地将日记描述为“回忆录文学最原始的形式”，是一连串“个人条目之间的分子联系”，仅由“叙述者的统一性”维系在一起。见《回忆录文学》（“Memuarnaia literatura”），载《文学百科全书》（Literaturnaia entsiklopediia），第7卷（莫斯科：共产主义科学院出版社，1934年），第131–139栏。
en:
Bouvard, “Le moi au miroir,” 85. An encyclopedia article of the period
praised the memoir’s ability to organize an author’s life “through the
prism of a specific ideological concept” and disdainfully character-
ized the diary as the “most primitive form of memoir literature,” a
chain of “molecular link[s] between individual entries,” held together
only by the “narrator’s unity.” “Memuarnaia literatura,” in Literatur-
naia entsiklopediia, vol. 7 (Moscow: Izd-vo Kommunisticheskoi aka-
demii, 1934), col. 131–139.

zh: 日记写作似乎在革命前的社会主义运动中得到了广泛实践。批评家和作家车尔尼雪夫斯基和尼古拉·多布罗留波夫——许多革命者都以他们的形象塑造自己——保留了内省和自我完善的日记记录。见帕佩尔诺著，《车尔尼雪夫斯基与现实主义时代》；O. G. 叶戈罗夫（O. G. Egorov）著，《19世纪俄罗斯作家日记研究》（Dnevniki russkikh pisatelei XIX veka. Issledovanie）（莫斯科：弗林塔出版社，2002年）。20世纪10年代一部小说中的社会民主主义英雄写了一本日记，他为日记设计的封面上有艘希腊三层划桨战船在“我的希望”标题下漂浮。每一只桨上“都刻着‘劳动’。带有方形帆的桅杆中央出现了‘自由’。桅杆顶端是一面印有‘理想’格言的旗帜。船尾可以辨认出三层战船的名字：‘生活’；船身两侧镶嵌着两块宽大的牌匾，上面写着 ‘科学’和‘战斗’。船的舵被称为‘意志力’。”见莫吉尔纳著，《地下人神话》，第101页。
en:
Diary-writing appears to have been widely practiced in the prerevo-
lutionary socialist movement. The critics and writers Chernyshev-
skii and Nikolai Dobroliubov, in whose image many revolutionaries
molded themselves, kept diaristic records of introspection and self-
improvement. See Paperno, Chernyshevsky and the Age of Realism; O. G.
Egorov, Dnevniki russkikh pisatelei XIX veka. Issledovanie (Moscow:
Flinta, 2002). The social-democratic hero of a novel from the 1910s
kept a diary for which he designed a cover featuring a Greek trireme
floating beneath the caption “my hopes.” Each oar “was inscribed
with the word labor. In the center of the mast with a quadrangular
sail appeared the inscription liberty. At the top of the mast was a flag
with the motto ideal. On the stern the name of the trireme could
be discerned: life; and two wide plaques set into the flanks of the
ship read science and battle. The helm of the ship was called will-
power.” Mogil’ner, Mif o podpol’nom cheloveke, 101.

zh: 富尔曼诺夫著，《全集》，第4卷，第214页（1919年12月29日）。尼古拉二世的日记发表在《红色档案馆》（Krasnyi arkhiv），1927年第1–3期；1928年第2期。
en:
Furmanov, Sobranie sochinenii, vol. 4, 214 (12/29/1919). The diary of
Nicholas II was published in Krasnyi arkhiv, 1927, no. 1–3; 1928, no. 2.

zh: 引自哈霍尔丁著，《俄罗斯的集体与个人》，第254–255页。
en: Cited in Kharkhordin, Collective and Individual in Russia, 254–255.

zh: 见奥列格·哈霍尔丁著，《揭示与掩饰：苏俄私生活的谱系》（“Reveal and Dissimulate: A Genealogy of Private Life in Soviet Russia”），载《思想与实践中的公共与私人》（Public and Private in Thought and Practice），杰夫·温特劳布（Jeff Weintraub）与克里尚·库马尔（Krishan Kumar）编（芝加哥：芝加哥大学出版社，1994年）；瓦迪姆·沃尔科夫（Vadim Volkov）著，《“文化性”概念：斯大林主义文明化进程笔记》（“The Concept of Kul’turnost’: Notes on the Stalinist Civilizing Process”），载《斯大林主义：新方向》（Stalinism: New Directions），希拉·菲茨帕特里克编（伦敦：劳特利奇出版社，1999年）。
en:
See Oleg Kharkhordin, “Reveal and Dissimulate: A Genealogy of Pri-
vate Life in Soviet Russia,” in Public and Private in Thought and Practice,
ed. Jeff Weintraub and Krishan Kumar (Chicago: University of Chi-
cago Press, 1994); Vadim Volkov, “The Concept of Kul’turnost’: Notes
on the Stalinist Civilizing Process,” in Stalinism: New Directions, ed.
Sheila Fitzpatrick (London: Routledge, 1999).

zh: 这种转变可以在伊利亚·爱伦堡（Il’ia Erenburg）的小说《第二天》中找到踪迹，该书于1933年首次出版。爱伦堡与其他的苏联小说家（尤其是富尔曼诺夫和费奥多尔·格拉德科夫）决裂，后者将共产主义英雄塑造为日记作者。在爱伦堡的小说中，反派瓦夏·萨福诺夫是一个病态的孤独者，他写秘密日记，倾诉他的反革命思想。见伊利亚·爱伦堡著，《第二天》（Den’ vtoroi. Roman，巴黎：帕斯卡出版社，1933年）；费奥多尔·格拉德科夫著，《能量》（Energiia，莫斯科：苏联文学出版社，1933年）。
en:
This transition can be traced in Il’ia Erenburg’s novel Second Day,
first published in 1933. Erenburg breaks with other Soviet novelists
(notably Furmanov and Fedor Gladkov) who featured Communist
heroes as diarists. In Erenburg’s novel a villain, Vasia Safonov, a
morbid loner, keeps a secret diary to which he confides his counter-
revolutionary thoughts; Il’ia Erenburg, Den’ vtoroi. Roman (Paris:
Pascal, 1933); Fedor Gladkov, Energiia (Moscow: Sovetskaia literatura,
1933).

zh: 见第3章讨论的奥尔加·别尔戈尔茨（Ol’ga Berggol’ts）的日记。
en: See the diary of Ol’ga Berggol’ts, discussed in Chapter 3.

zh: 《“工会运动瓦解的开始”：B. G. 科泽列夫日记（1927–1930）》（“‘Nachalo razgroma profdvizheniia.’ Dnevnik B. G. Kozeleva. 1927–1930 gg.”），载《历史档案馆》（Istoricheskii arkhiv），1996年第5–6期；1997年第1期。在日记的后记（写于1991年）中，科泽列夫的女儿指出，中央委员会委派她的父亲去马格尼托哥尔斯克。鉴于他早先决定成为一名工厂工人的决定——这是共产党人应对退化指控的一种经典方式——很可能是他自己申请加入这场社会主义战斗。
en:
“‘Nachalo razgroma profdvizheniia.’ Dnevnik B. G. Kozeleva. 1927–
1930 gg.,” in Istoricheskii arkhiv, 1996, no. 5–6; 1997, no. 1. In an after-
word to the diary (written in 1991), Kozelev’s daughter notes that the
Central Committee commissioned her father to go to Magnitogorsk.
In view of his earlier decision to become a factory worker—a classical
way Communists responded to charges of degeneration—it is likely
that he himself applied to join the battle for socialism.

zh: N. 佩图霍夫（N. Petukhov）与 V. 霍姆奇克（V. Khomchik）著，《关于“列宁格勒中心”案》（“Delo o ‘Leningradskom tsentre’”），载《苏联最高法院公报》（Vestnik Verkhovnogo Suda SSSR），1991年第5期，第15–18页；阿拉·基里琳娜（Alla Kirilina）著，《不为人知的基洛夫》（Neizvestnyi Kirov）（圣彼得堡：“涅瓦”出版社，2001年）。

N. Petukhov and V. Khomchik, “Delo o ‘Leningradskom tsentre’,”
